summary: Customer (MediVault) is evaluating Redwood for sensitive PHI-adjacent workloads and needs clear data residency guarantees, region pinning, and BYOK/KMS options. Discussed cross-border processing, sub-processor list, RBAC/SSO, audit logs and retention. Agreed to share SOC2 artifacts, architecture diagram for region pinning, and coordinate a pilot in Jan.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-20 15:30 UTC | Duration: ~52 minutes | Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Laura Gomez (MediVault Head of Security), Tom Becker (Platform Eng), Ellen Ruiz (Compliance)

[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining on a friday afternoon, appreciate you making time. quick roll call?
[00:10] Laura Gomez: yes, laura here.
[00:12] Tom Becker: tom here.
[00:14] Ellen Ruiz: ellen here.
[00:16] Priya Nair: priya from redwood, hi all.
[00:20] Alex Chen: great. objective for today is to walk through data residency / region pinning and cover KMS / sub-processor concerns, also SOC2 and audit logs.
[01:05] Laura Gomez: high level we run patient-adjacent data, not PHI per se but regulated; our legal team is strict on cross-border transfers, so we need guarantees that eu customer data stays in eu, no fallback to us regions unless we approve.
[01:40] Priya Nair: totally understood. quick overview: redwood supports region pinning — requests can be routed to EU-only clusters and we can scope a tenant to run exclusively in eu-west or eu-central. fallback behavior is configurable, default is no cross-border fallback for pinned tenants.
[02:30] Tom Becker: when you say "pinned to eu-west" is that at the tenant level or per-endpoint? we have multiple services per tenant and some ingest pipelines live in us for analytics, want to be granular.
[02:50] Priya Nair: good q — we do tenant-level pinning by default, but we also support per-route pinning. for your use case we can pin the model serving and inference pipelines to eu while allowing telemetry metrics to flow to a central us analytics cluster if you opt in — that opt-in is manual and auditable.
[03:45] Ellen Ruiz: and subprocessors — which cloud providers or vendors have access to eu data? our procurement needs a list to run through their DPA.
[04:05] Alex Chen: we can provide a subprocessors list; common ones: aws (eu regions), google cloud (europe), datadog (metrics), fastly/akamai or cloudflare (cdn), segment (if used), and internal observability teams. we'll send the canonical list and timestamps of when data is replicated.
[04:45] Laura Gomez: replication — do you replicate to us for durability or backups? that is a non-starter for us unless encrypted and with contractual controls.
[05:10] Priya Nair: by default regional clusters are self-contained. for backups we can configure encrypted snapshots stored in-region only. cross-region replication is off for pinned tenants unless you enable an explicit disaster-recovery config which we can document and lock behind approvals.
[05:45] Tom Becker: KMS — can you support BYOK or HSM-backed keys? we want to manage encryption keys for at-rest to satisfy our security policies.
[06:05] Priya Nair: yes, we support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and HSM integrations for the private deployments. for hosted tenants we offer BYOK where you keep the master key in your KMS and we encrypt with a data key that your KMS wraps. we also do key rotation and a KMS audit trail.
[06:50] Ellen Ruiz: is there an option for offline key escrow or do you hold any key material?
[07:05] Alex Chen: Redwood does not hold customer master keys if you opt for BYOK. We may have ephemeral data keys in memory for processing — they are never written to disk and are rotated frequently. we can provide architecture diagrams and HSM attestation info.
[07:50] Laura Gomez: audit logs — we need immutable audit trails for all api calls, plus export to our SIEM in eu. retention 7 years preferred. what are your options?
[08:10] Priya Nair: audit logs are configurable. we provide tenant-level audit logs, Admin actions, token issuance, and data access events. logs can be shipped to your S3/GCS bucket in eu or pushed to your SIEM (we support syslog/forwarders). retention defaults to 90 days but we offer extended retention tiers — there's a storage cost tradeoff.
[09:00] Tom Becker: is the audit log export encrypted in transit? do you sign logs?
[09:15] Priya Nair: yes TLS 1.3 for transport, and we support signed log exports with an optional envelope signature.
[09:35] Laura Gomez: SOC2 — do you have current certification and can you share the attestations?
[09:45] Alex Chen: we are SOC 2 Type II certified — we'll send the report under NDA; also have ISO27001 in progress. we'll attach the last audit date in the doc we send.
[10:12] Ellen Ruiz: great. also need a DPIA and clarity on processors in eu — sample DPA?
[10:25] Alex Chen: yes we'll include the DPA and sample contract clauses; we have a standard DPA and a list of subprocessors with locations.
[10:40] Tom Becker: one thing on cross-border: sometimes model weights or updates are stored in centralized model registry. are those registries replicated? could a model pull from a us bucket at runtime?
[11:05] Priya Nair: good point. models are versioned and can be pinned to region. if you request a model that's only available in us, we'll return a mismatch. for your setup we can seed a region-local copy of the model and pin the runtime to it — that avoids cross-border pulls. we'll document the model vetting process.
[12:00] Laura Gomez: what's your support for SSO/SCIM? we need RBAC with separate admin roles and SCIM user provisioning.
[12:20] Alex Chen: SSO via SAML or OIDC is supported; SCIM provisioning for user accounts is available to enterprise customers. RBAC includes admin, operator, reader roles plus custom roles; we can map to your groups.
[12:50] Ellen Ruiz: any out-of-band admin APIs that bypass tenant restrictions? we need assurance there are no hidden super-admin bypasses that could access eu data.
[13:10] Priya Nair: access is strictly logged; super-admin actions are audited and require two-person review for certain operations. For private deployments we can disable remote support access unless explicitly enabled.
[13:45] Tom Becker: network-level — peering options? we operate inside our vpc, want private connectivity.
[13:58] Priya Nair: we support VPC peering, private link, and on-prem connectors for private deployments. for hosted we have private endpoints and can enable dedicated capacity (redwood dedicated) inside a customer vpc in some regions.
[14:30] Laura Gomez: incident response — SLA for notifications? our policy requires 72-hour initial notification and follow-ups.
[14:45] Alex Chen: our incident response policy meets that; we do 72-hour notification for incidents involving data exposure and have a dedicated incident manager for enterprise accounts.
transcript_continued:
[15:30] Ellen Ruiz: regarding subprocessors — are you willing to add restrictions for specific vendors? our legal flagged fastly as a concern.
[15:50] Alex Chen: we can discuss vendor restrictions in the DPA negotiation; some vendors are mandatory for network delivery, others are optional. we'll highlight alternatives in the subprocessor list.
[16:20] Tom Becker: scalability/latency: if we pin to eu, do we see any performance impact compared to us region?
[16:35] Priya Nair: performance is tied to region capacity; eu regions are comparable but peak hours differ. we can provision dedicated capacity to guarantee latency SLOs for your traffic.
[17:10] Laura Gomez: compliance proof — any demo of logs export workflow?
[17:20] Priya Nair: yes, priya to run a short demo in the technical deep dive; we'll show audit export to an eu s3 and SIEM ingest.
[18:00] Alex Chen: just to capture risks: cross-border fallback, BYOK misconfig, subprocessor changes without notice — we will add controls and sign-off gates.
[18:30] Ellen Ruiz: on subprocessor notifications, do you provide 30/60 day notice of changes?
[18:45] Alex Chen: standard is 30 days; critical changes we surface earlier in critical incidents.
[19:05] Laura Gomez: data residency enforcement — is it policy-based or enforced at the network layer? can we get an attestation?
[19:25] Priya Nair: it's enforced at orchestration layer and network routing; we can provide a technical attestation for the implementation and screenshots of routing rules for the pilot tenant.
[20:05] Tom Becker: for the pilot, we want a small workload pinned to eu, BYOK with our aws kms key, audit logs exported to our eu bucket, and a 30-day retention.
[20:30] Alex Chen: that works. we'll scope pilot: duration 4 weeks, goals: verify no cross-border egress, key lifecycle validation, and log integrity.
[21:00] Ellen Ruiz: what about data subject requests & deletions? if a european user asks for erasure, how are logs and cached content handled?
[21:20] Priya Nair: we have delete APIs that purge tenant data and user data from primary stores; logs are immutable but can be redacted with retention policy; cached KV caches have TTLs and can be evicted on request. we'll detail the erasure flow.
[22:05] Laura Gomez: legal will want the DPA + subprocessors before we sign; technical will want the deep dive.
[22:25] Alex Chen: action items recap: alex will send SOC2 + DPA draft; priya will share region pinning diagram and BYOK steps; tom/ellen to confirm acceptance criteria.
[22:45] Laura Gomez: thanks, wrap up. good session.
[23:00] Alex Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with docs and next steps.
